R<sup>2</sup>D emerged from a long-running research program in muscle,
molecular motors, thermodynamics, and multiscale biological mechanics.
The conventional scientific record of that work and the developing
R<sup>2</sup>D archive serve different purposes.

## Muscle and Molecular Motor Research

For more than two decades, my research has examined how molecular-scale
events become mechanical behavior at the scale of muscle.

This work includes the molecular mechanisms of muscle contraction and
regulation, the mechanochemistry of myosin molecular motors, muscle
thermodynamics, ensemble mechanics, single-molecule and whole-cell
measurements, and multiscale models of biological systems.

A recurring question has been how randomly fluctuating molecular motors
can collectively generate the deterministic force, shortening, and power
measured at the scale of a muscle fiber.

That question ultimately led beyond muscle. Muscle provides an unusually
useful scientific system because chemistry, thermodynamics, statistical
mechanics, and mechanics can all be measured on the same physical system
while the definition of the scientific object changes with scale.

The peer-reviewed publications documenting this research program can be
found through Google Scholar.

[VIEW PUBLICATIONS ON GOOGLE SCHOLAR →](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=uofIPKMAAAAJ&hl=en){target="_blank"}


## From Muscle to R<sup>2</sup>D

The development of R<sup>2</sup>D began with a problem exposed by muscle:
the mathematics that describes a muscle fiber cannot simply be assigned
to one of its subordinate molecular components.

A myosin molecule and a muscle fiber are different scientific objects.
Each has its own states, transitions, constraints, and readable
observables.

R<sup>2</sup>D formalizes this boundary dependence by defining microstate
and macrostate at the boundary where they are distinguished. Changing
scale therefore does not merely coarse-grain the same object. It changes
the mathematical state domain and, with it, the object being described.

The resulting framework has since been developed beyond muscle into a
general mathematical interface for examining scientific structure across
physics, chemistry, biology, and geometry.


## R<sup>2</sup>D Archive and Continuing Development

Formal versions of R<sup>2</sup>D are archived on Zenodo.

Zenodo provides permanent, citable records of the framework at defined
stages of development. These archived releases include the R<sup>2</sup>D
Canon and subsequent formal developments and applications.

The distinction between the archive and this website is intentional:

- **Zenodo preserves fixed scholarly versions.**
- **R2DScience.org presents the current framework and makes it easier to navigate and use.**
- **The Canon remains the authoritative mathematical source.**
- **Applications show how the framework develops when it is run against specific scientific problems.**

As R<sup>2</sup>D develops, major formal releases will continue to be
deposited on Zenodo so that earlier formulations remain permanently
available and citable.

[VIEW THE R²D ARCHIVE ON ZENODO →](https://zenodo.org/me/uploads?q=&f=shared_with_me%3Afalse&l=list&p=1&s=10&sort=newest){target="_blank"}


## Current Canon

The current Canon is the master statement of the R<sup>2</sup>D
framework.

It is intended both for human readers and as a source document for AI.
Future releases will be made available in formats suitable for reading,
archiving, and machine interrogation.

[READ THE CANON →](https://zenodo.org/records/22760358)
